requirement: During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to its declaration or within its body. A named example MUST cite a requirement. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count. Habeas MUST report every uncited function with its file, line, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.
rationale:
I judge the requirement satisfied. I reviewed the supplied excerpts and did not run the tests or the self-validation, so this rests on reading the code and the test assertions.

**Implementation (`src/rust_coverage.rs`, wired in at `src/evidence.rs` `inspect_repository_with_progress`)**
- `rust_files` walks the whole project. It skips only `.git`, `target`, and the root-level `book`, `evidence`, and `vendor` directories. Walk, read, and entry errors are reported rather than ignored.
- `validate_rust_functions` reads each file and calls `missing_function_references`. That function uses `syn::parse_file` and a `FunctionCollector` visitor. The visitor covers free functions, impl methods, trait methods (including bodiless ones), and foreign functions, and it recurses so nested functions are found too.
- A parse failure is pushed as `file:line: cannot parse Rust source`, so a file is never silently skipped. An unreadable file is likewise reported.
- A custom lexer, `comments()`, finds only real comments. It uses `quoted_end`, `char_end`, and `raw_string_end` to skip string, raw-string, and char literals. This excludes references inside string literals.
- `attached_comment_indices` attaches the contiguous comment block directly before a declaration, including through attributes, because the item span includes them. It stops at inner doc comments, trailing comments on a previous code line, blank-line gaps, and non-comment text. A comment on an enclosing module or impl block therefore does not cover the functions inside it.
- A comment inside a body belongs to the smallest enclosing function. An inner function's comment does not cover the outer function.
- A function counts as cited only if some owned comment holds a non-`term` role (`impl`, `cite`, or `test`) whose name resolves to a defined non-term requirement or example. Unknown names do not count.
- Each uncited function is reported as `file:line: function name has no requirement or example citation`.
- Evidence inputs are never consulted, so a citation that appears only there cannot count.

**Tests**
- `finds_uncited_functions_without_using_enclosing_or_string_references` covers:
  - enclosing mod and impl citations that must not count;
  - string and raw-string literals, and a char `'/'`;
  - an unknown requirement name;
  - a citation inside the body (block comment);
  - a distant comment separated by a blank line;
  - a trailing comment on the previous line;
  - inner doc comments;
  - an outer doc comment that does count.
- `checks_trait_test_helper_and_nested_functions_separately` covers trait methods, nested functions, `{test}` on a requirement, `{test}` on a named example, and an uncited test helper.
- `locates_functions_after_unicode_text` checks byte-offset and line correctness after non-ASCII text.
- `reports_all_files_and_parse_failures` checks multi-file reporting with file, line, and name. It also checks that a parse failure is reported, and that `target/` and `evidence/` are excluded.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs` checks that a parse failure on `src/lib.rs` surfaces from the CLI.
- `tests/commands.rs` checks that the uncited-function message reaches `habeas status` output.

**Gaps**
- Functions generated inside macro invocation bodies are not visible to `syn`. This fits the "explicitly declared" wording.
- I found no FIXME markers.
- The coverage is thorough for the design space of the requirement.

A false or FIXME determination MUST have its distinct state when the record passes all other checks. The FIXME state MUST pass validation while retaining its distinct label. Each evidence detail page MUST display its state as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text and the current requirement or example body as a Markdown block quote labeled by kind. Each input MUST have its own subsection identifying its selector. A file-range or Rust-item input MUST show its resolved file and inclusive line range. Its `determination` MUST remain a boolean assessing citation coverage; the FIXME outcome applies to requirement and example judgments. Its `citations` MUST be the nonempty set of valid references owned by the function, each recorded by role and full requirement or example name. Its `inputs` MUST include one Rust-item input selecting the function and at least one requirements input; together, the requirements inputs MUST match every name in `citations`. Habeas MUST validate every input and fail for a missing, duplicate, orphaned, stale, or false attestation, a changed citation set, or an empty rationale. Each finding MUST identify the source file, current line when available, and item selector.

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references.

In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.targets`.

For every `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` reference in a project source file, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.

During repository validation, Habeas MUST parse every first-party Rust source file in the project. Every explicitly declared function or method, including trait methods and test helpers, MUST have a valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference to a defined requirement or named example in a Rust comment attached to its declaration or within its body. A named example MUST cite a requirement. A reference in a string literal, on an enclosing module or impl block, or only in an evidence input MUST NOT count. Habeas MUST report every uncited function with its file, line, and name, and MUST report a Rust parse failure instead of silently skipping the file.

A definition glob MUST match a complete full name. `*` MUST match zero or more characters, including dots; all other valid name characters MUST match literally. An empty glob MUST be invalid. The same glob matching rule MUST be used by requirements evidence inputs and CLI definition filters. All three MUST match against both requirements and named examples.

Habeas MUST identify a Rust item by the pair of its `rust_file`, following the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, and a `rust_item` selector derived from a `syn` parse of that file. The selector MUST describe syntactic ancestry within the file and MUST NOT resolve Rust modules across files or use line numbers as identity. Named items MUST use kind-and-name segments such as `fn[run]` and `struct[Packet]`. Impl segments MUST distinguish inherent from trait impls using their syntactic self type and optional trait path. Otherwise identical selectors MUST have deterministic source-order disambiguators. A `use` declaration MUST have a positional selector `use#N`, where N is its one-based position among sibling `use` declarations; its import target MUST NOT form part of the selector. Other items without a suitable name MUST have a kind and positional disambiguator. Selector spelling MUST be documented and reversible when names or types contain delimiter characters.
